operations.name: Barncho

expected.name: Barncho
expected.description: Barncho was a combatant in the Modoc War (1872–1873) — the only Indigenous fighters in U.S. history convicted as "war criminals" by a U.S. military commission for their role in the killing of Brigadier General Edward Canby during peace negotiations at the Lava Beds on April 11, 1873. The Modoc had resisted forced removal from their California ancestral lands to the Klamath Reservation in Oregon for years before the war. Sentenced to life imprisonment and held at Alcatraz federal military prison.

operations.source: https://www.nps.gov/articles/the-army-and-american-indian-prisoners.htm — National Park Service account explicitly dates Barncho’s death at Alcatraz May 28, 1875. Corroborated by https://www.opb.org/article/2025/05/28/southern-oregon-modoc-alcatraz-prison-history-native-americans-indigenous/ . This is death in custody, not a release date; admission remains unresolved.

operations.name: John Sinclair

expected.sentence:
9½ to 10 years in state prison. Released on bond December 13, 1971 — three days after the "Free John Sinclair" rally at Ann Arbor's Crisler Arena (John Lennon, Yoko Ono, Stevie Wonder, Allen Ginsberg, Bob Seger, Phil Ochs and others, before 15,000 people) — after serving about 29 months.

Verdict as recorded: Convicted July 1969. The conviction was overturned by the Michigan Supreme Court on March 9, 1972 (People v. Sinclair), which struck down the state's marijuana statute as unconstitutional.

Charges as recorded: Possession of marijuana — for giving two joints to undercover Detroit narcotics officers in December 1966 (his third marijuana charge).

operations.source: https://www.fifthestate.org/archive/85-august-7-20-1969/the-crime-and-punishment-of-john-sinclair/ — contemporary August 7–20, 1969 report explicitly names Judge Robert J. Colombo at July 28, 1969 sentencing. Applies to the existing 1967 marijuana case; no dates imported into the separate 1966 case.

operations.name: Hercules Anderson

expected.name: Hercules Anderson
expected.description: Hercules Anderson was one of four Black land-reclamation protesters arrested by federal marshals at Harris Neck, Georgia, on May 1, 1979. The protesters occupied land that the federal government had taken from a Black community during World War II and refused an order to leave. A federal judge convicted them of criminal contempt on May 4 and imposed thirty days in jail. They spent more than fifteen days in the Savannah jail, but their exact release dates and the amount of the thirty-day sentence ultimately served have not been located.

operations.source: https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/thebrunswicknews/name/hercules-anderson-obituary?id=25049336 — family-placed obituary in The Brunswick News, October 7, 2021, identifies Hercules Anderson of Harris Neck and explicitly dates death October 3, 2021. Harris Neck identity matches the land-reclamation activist; no inference from unrelated same-name records.
